faq.q: What should I write in my journal?
faq.a: Write one thing from today that is still on your mind, what you felt about it, and why you think it affected you. A 2002 study by Ullrich and Lutgendorf found that journaling about both thoughts and feelings worked better than writing about feelings alone.

faq.q: How long should a journal entry be?
faq.a: A few lines is enough, and one line counts. In a 2008 study by Burton and King, writing for two minutes on two days was linked to fewer health complaints weeks later. A 2023 meta-analysis found the number of sessions mattered less than writing again within one to three days.

faq.q: What do you write in a journal when nothing happened?
faq.a: Write the ordinary day anyway: one sensory detail, one conversation, or a mood word and a guess at its cause. Harvard researchers found people underestimate how interesting their mundane moments will be to reread months later.

faq.q: Should I use journal prompts or write freely?
faq.a: Either works. In a 2023 meta-analysis of expressive writing, the type of instructions did not change the benefit. Prompts help most when the blank page is the problem, as long as they are about your actual day and don't pull you into the same worry again.

faq.q: How do I start journaling as a beginner?
faq.a: Tie it to something you already do in the evening, write one-line notes during the day, and spend five minutes at night on what happened, what you felt and why. After a week, reread your entries and keep the formats that felt easy.

informationGain: Where the top results offer unsourced idea lists, this piece gives seven concrete formats with example entries, each tied to the study that tested it (Ullrich and Lutgendorf on feeling plus meaning, Burton and King's two-minute dose, Guo on spacing over length, Zhang on rereading ordinary days, the Day Reconstruction Method, Three Good Things with its sobering replication, Kross on third-person self-talk, Scullin's to-do list), and answers how short an entry can be and what to write on a blank day with evidence.
